question: Open questions of NEP-0005 (#1763): how do Windows Filtering Platform (WFP) filter sets that are only part of the srt-win four-object set, and sets we build ourselves, behave for a throwaway account's loopback connects on IPv4 and IPv6; what does srt-win's own status word say for each; and can that account's standard (non-elevated) token add or delete a filter?

hardware.gpu: not relevant to this measurement (no GPU or model work)
hardware.os: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, display version 25H2, update build revision 9457 (read 2026-10-13 10:56)
hardware.host_shell_per_proof: PowerShell 7.6.6 (ConsoleHost, Core) as recorded by the rollback proof

software.halfset_rs_sha256_note: hash of the bytes that were built and ran; the bundled copy docs/research/containment-evidence-2026-10-05/nep0005-open-questions/harness/halfset.rs hashes cbd6ad65760bf2f297a35c5330f7ca23b0ef5339098f0818a3c910b227be7b2c since 2026-10-13, when its three SID constants were rewritten from the real machine domain to the placeholder domain (#1765); nothing else changed

antivirus: Bitdefender processes present when read at 10:58 the same day (bdagent, bdntwrk, bdredline, bdservicehost, bduserhost); state during the runs not recorded
method: Throwaway local account blarai-spike (relative id 1271). Per state and pass: direct sweep of three test sublayers (S1 srt-win harness, S2 ours, S3 ours) and a netsh export must read clean; control (account and operator connect to six loopback targets before any filter); add the state; record srt-win status, enumeration and our key reads; account connects to six targets (127.0.0.1 and [::1] at ports 61763, 61764, 60085 where 60085 is inside the srt-win permit range 60080-60089); remove by key; sweep again. Three passes per state, back to back. Account probes ran through a secondary (interactive-type) logon with a fresh in-memory session password, not the task's batch logon. N1: the account's own standard token makes one direct FwpmFilterAdd0 and one direct FwpmFilterDeleteByKey0 against S2.

results.post_state_direct_checks: clean after removal in 45 of 45 cycles (42 connect cycles and 3 N1): S1, S2, S3 0 filters and sublayers absent, provider absent, export hits 0, no foreign filter

R2.title: V4 block deleted (V6 block and both permits remain)

R3.title: V6 block deleted (V4 block and both permits remain)

R6.title: stale: full set for the stale test SID

R7.title: S3: our unlabelled blocks for the account; srt-win status read on S1 (empty)

O3.title: S2 set: permit without a block

O4.title: S2 set: both blocks + an exact-port permit (127.0.0.1, no user condition)

O5.title: S2: a block with no provider, attempted (the engine's answer is the result)

O6.title: a filter naming a missing sublayer, attempted (the engine's answer is the result)

N1.title: non-elevated add and delete by the account's own standard token against S2

exports.taken: before adding and after removal only

not_measured: any target beyond loopback (no internet address, no other host)
UDP, DNS and other ports than 61763, 61764 and 60085
persistence: each state stood seconds; no restart, hold or sleep
variation across boots or days (three back-to-back passes on one boot)
the batch-logon token of the account's scheduled task under these states
the Network Configuration Operators row (not run)
whether the session was elevated, the launch command lines, other machine load and the Bitdefender state during the runs (not recorded)
replication_note: Three passes per state ran minutes apart on one boot and agreed in every state; that is a repeat, not independent replication. No variation across conditions was measured.
